newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: AfDB arrears to fall "substantially" in 1997.
newsitem.headline: AfDB arrears to fall "substantially" in 1997.

text.p: The total arrears owed by African countries to the African Development Bank (AfDB) should fall substantially in 1997, the Bank's treasurer said on Thursday.

"The mechanisms put in place to reduce the arrears have already shown their effectiveness -- in 1996 by cutting the rhythm at which they progressed, and above all in 1997 when the volume of arrears should be reduced substantially," Thierry de Longuemar told Reuters.
He was speaking at the end of the Bank's annual meeting, where the arrears issue was raised by several speakers.
De Longuemar said they had not taken into account the progress made this year in particular, when Congo, Cameroon, Niger and Madagascar had all paid off their arrears.
Another country is about to do the same, he said, but declined to name it until arrangements were complete.
The bulk of the arrears is owed by countries going through political or social strife.

By far the biggest sum is owed by the Democratic Republic of Congo, formerly Zaire, with 329 million units of account, or around $474 million, in arrears at the end of 1996, when the total owed by 11 countries came to 576 million units of account.
The other countries with significant arrears at that time were Congo, Angola, Liberia and, to a lesser extent, Somalia, according to the annual report.
